about: Which text of business records search indexes. The rule: every text-valued property (schema value_type in rule.value_types) of every served or partial object type is indexed, so a new type is covered without an entry here. Exceptions are explicit: deny (only ids, hashes and secrets, by full-match name pattern), and documents (types whose text a document chunker indexes: mail, attachment, SharePoint, Teams, Mission Control, meeting; each property listed as text the document chunk carries or as fields_only, a closed code read by plx.find filters). json_fields: JSON properties whose string leaves are indexed as 'Column: value' lines (SharePoint list item columns). A value is chunked when it is wordy: label properties (names, titles, subjects, descriptions, notes, comments) from label_min_chars, every other property from min_chars, both with min_letter_share letters. Numbers in indexed text are never truth: the record answers. Markings: a chunk carries the union of its value's markings and the record's current and latest version markings.

deny_about.ids: Identifiers, keys, handles, links, contact addresses, phone numbers and bank or tax registration numbers (substring patterns, matched on the lower-cased name, list columns included): found through plx.find identifiers and the identity resolver, never by text search. Whatever a field is called, a value that looks like an email address or a phone number is masked before it is chunked.

never_text.about: Free text of Sage GL, AR and AP records (descriptions, references, comments, text lines, memos, notes) names staff on pay documents (payroll, wage, salary, commission and bonus lines): never search text, whatever a reader holds. AR customer comments (RelSageArCmm, credit-handling notes) keep their reviewed indexing. Matches lane/mega's text_markings rule (reviews of lane raw-tables, 2026-11-08).
Customer, vendor and remitter name columns of Sage GL lines say who a pay line paid: never search text (lane/mega, 2026-11-08).

Who did or owns a thing (actors, creators, completers, approvers, requesters, organizers, owners, assignees): a person, said as a name, an address or a directory object id. A person is found through the identity resolver under the people exclusion, never by text search; Planner's created_by/completed_by are directory object ids (lane search-cov-1113, 2026-11-13).

words_only.about: Record text that is not human language (codes, references, mostly digits or punctuation, short upper-case refs) is word-indexed as kind record_words and never sent to embedding: a free-text value embeds when it holds at least min_words words of at least 3 letters that are not short upper-case codes and min_letter_share of letters; a label value (a name or title) when it holds one such word. Every raw relation type (Rel*: Sage, silver, BC, Portal and FileMaker raw rows; names full-matching raw_types) is words-only whatever its text: only business types and human-language text are embedded.

card.about: Every business record gets one words-only card (kind record_words, never embedded): its type, its identifiers and its short text values (status, codes, currency, carrier, at most max_value_chars) that no chunk of its own carries, so a record of any type is found by its numbers and state (lane search-cov-1113, 2026-11-13: most Portal and BC records held no searchable text because every text value was shorter than min_chars). A record with no business identifier gets none (its card would be every such record's, one cluster in search). Only values and identifiers the record's own markings cover; never a figure (only text properties the rule reads); keyed by the record's unit and markings, cited to its current version. Raw mirror rows (except_types) get none: their business types carry the card.
